newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. keeps Australian bonds easier ahead of jobs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. keeps Australian bonds easier ahead of jobs.

text.p: *Australian bonds maintain their easier tone through the morning, most notably at long end, as U.S. Treasuries retain heavier tone on quarterly refunding supply concerns.
*Market waiting on Thursday's labour force figures.

"That's certainly adding a bit of weakness, a bit of uncertainty on what's happening in the States, in terms of our long end, and we're just waiting on the employment numbers tomorrow," one trader said.
Australian bonds extended their weaker opening tone through a dour morning session, with the weakness ahead of Thursday's key labour market data attributed to softness in the U.S. Treasuries market.

The U.S. market received the first tranche of this week's $38 million quarterly refunding auctions last night which, when combined with signs of steengthening economic activity, saw Treasuries retain a softer bias in Asian trading.
While the local July employment data was expected to be bond-friendly, traders said in the absence of other leads until then the U.S. market would remain a weight on bonds.
Long end spreads widen as long bonds ease from opening levels as morning progresses. Curve retains a steepening bias.
